hooks.name: Refresh handoff
hooks.description: At the end of a session, rewrite .kiro/steering/handoff.md in one pass so the next session starts with accurate state. Defers to the document protocol in project.md for all limits.

action.prompt:
If this session changed no file, leave `.kiro/steering/handoff.md` alone and say so. If it is already accurate and current, leave it alone — re-writing an accurate file is pure cost.

Otherwise rewrite it to describe the CURRENT state only, and follow the "Document protocol" section of `.kiro/steering/project.md`, which is the authority on this file. Do not restate or second-guess its limits from here.

Three rules from that protocol matter most, because breaking them is what has cost real tokens before:

1. **ONE write.** Compose the whole file and write it once. Never edit last session's copy down line by line — that turned a single operation into twelve round trips and cost several times what the file itself costs to carry.
2. **State and pointers, never reasoning.** Where we are, what is next, what is blocked, what would bite, and WHERE the explanation lives. Reasoning goes in `project.md` if durable or `.tastemaker/style-lock.md` if visual. A handoff line that says *why* is duplicating something that already has a home, and that duplication is what made every previous version overrun.
3. **Size is a range, not a target to hit.** If it is over, delete a whole section or move it to its proper home. Never shave wording to reach a number.

Keep the section structure the current file uses rather than any list of headings you remember; it may legitimately have gained or lost one. Update the Last updated date. Anything durable that this session settled goes into `project.md` instead and stays out of the handoff.
